sentence: My uncle, who is the ______ of a small bakery, hires two students every summer. (employ)
explanation: We need a noun for a person who hires workers. The suffix -er creates a noun meaning someone who performs the action of the verb, so 'employ' becomes 'employer'. Turkish speakers may confuse 'employer' and 'employee' because both come from the same root with different suffixes; the -ee suffix marks the person who is employed.
